claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified now because aggregate readiness is positive and certification is defensible if the current packet/model-card update serves as the operative disclosure of the current health-plan benefits subgroup weakness required by policy.
decision_criteria: Does admissible evidence show the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results?
Does admissible evidence show the material segment weakness is disclosed in the current release documentation?
If not disclosed, is there an approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance covering it?
Are prior approvals and monitoring notes being used only as context, not as substitutes for current-release support?
Is the certification recommendation limited to what the evidence actually establishes?
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing the exact disclosed current evaluation results and the health-plan benefits segment weakness.
Provide evidence that this disclosure artifact is the reviewed and operative certification document for the current release.
Provide any approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the current subgroup weakness, if one exists.
Provide the materiality determination or threshold basis showing why this subgroup weakness does or does not require blocking certification absent mitigation.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation.
The Actor's own summary says the health-plan benefits slice is below the warning threshold and that prior approval did not include this regression.
The record, as summarized, does not show approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation for the current subgroup weakness.
Certification therefore turns on an unresolved predicate: whether the current packet/model-card update is in fact the operative current-release disclosure artifact.
Prior approval and informal monitoring are explicitly contextual only under the policy and do not substitute for current evidence or reviewed acceptance.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action to certify_model is not fully supported because there is no admissible evidence here proving the current release documentation actually contains the required disclosure.
Any implication that prior approval materially supports current certification beyond context is unsupported under the stated policy.
Any implication that informal post-launch monitoring closes the policy gap is unsupported because no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is shown.
